title: Why he disliked parade drumming
summary: He played parades only once or twice and disliked the walking; one was with Thomas Copeland for the carnival.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: Did you ever play in the drumming parades or funerals?
Once or twice, I never did like it.
You didn't like it, didn't care for it?
What didn't you like about it?
I just never did like it. For one thing, I didn't like the walking. The walking.
Did you play bass drum or snare drum on the stage?

I could play any of them, but I didn't care for them. I'm a daddy too, I just never did care for them. I played a parade twice. We played for the carnival, remember? With Thomas Copeland. Yeah. I played snare drum and what you call him?
We played for the Arabi packing company, the Arabi packing company. Maurice Duran, Thomas Copeland. Who's band running? Thomas Copeland.

I don't remember. Bass. He used to play bass. He used to play string bass with the Olympia band. Yeah. And all the Olympia band. After the first band, he played string bass with the band and he used to play his upright tuba.

Parade. It was his job, but it was really Maurice Duran's band. That's right. Tom Copeland used to get that job. Tom Copeland used to work at the Arabi packing companies. He'd cut meat. He used to get that job every day.

What you call him playing bass drum? What you call him? Parker, remember that? Big tall Parker. Parker. He died then. That was a good bass. He died then. Tom Parker. Tom Parker, yeah. That was a good one. I don't know.
He lived right in the block of the Caledonia. Yeah, I know. Yeah, that was a good one. Did he just play braids or did he play? Braids. There's some fella about, you know, I don't know.
